subject_line: Forty-two weeks of Friends from College
email_body:
Dear Devapriya,

I was interested to learn that Friends from College ran as a serial in The Telegraph for forty-two weeks before it became a novel, following old friends and lovers who meet again two decades after college. You've described it as a way of explaining your generation to younger readers.

I'd love to ask how writing in weekly instalments shaped the book, and what changed when you reworked it as a single novel.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions the author can answer at their own pace, and the full text is shared with them for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Friends from College serialised in The Telegraph for 42 weeks; The Edict (2024) interview on explaining her generation; Senior Writing Fellow at Ashoka (Sonipat). Email seen in search result from Ashoka faculty profile.

book_title: Modern Writers, Transnational Literatures: Rabindranath Tagore and W. B. Yeats
subject_line: Tagore, Yeats and the early international reception
email_body:
Dear Ragini,

I was struck by how Modern Writers, Transnational Literatures traces the relationship between Tagore and Yeats, and especially Tagore's early international reception, read through questions of identity, nationalism and the literary traditions of Ireland and India. I also noticed you returned to Yeats, Tagore and the Nobel Prize in a 2025 article.

I'd be curious to hear what first drew you to placing these two writers side by side.

subject_line: 关于《孕鱼》里的女性视角
email_body:
何颖舒老师,您好:

读到您的首部短篇小说集《孕鱼》以女性视角书写现代都市生活中隐秘的故事,并入围新加坡文学奖,很受触动。也注意到您在国大中文系教授创意写作,还创办了线上文学平台“读写岛计划”。

我很想请教:这些都市里不为人知的故事,通常是从哪里开始在您心里成形的?教写作又如何影响了您自己的写作?

The Author Ledger 是一个独立项目,专门刊登简短的作者专访。专访通过几个书面问题完成,作者可以按自己的节奏回答,全文在发表前会交由作者审阅。

不知您是否愿意参与?完全不必有压力。

此致敬礼,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Debut story collection 孕鱼 Fish Birth (2019), female perspective on hidden urban lives, shortlisted for Singapore Literature Prize; teaches creative writing at NUS Chinese Studies; founded 读写岛计划. Email seen in search result from NUS faculty page.
